prs.cluster_pick_reason: 3063 keys `_request_streams` by `str(message.id)`, which collapses JSON-RPC's distinct int `1` and string `"1"` ids into the same key and does nothing to stop a string id equal to `"_GET_stream"` from colliding with the reserved `GET_STREAM_KEY` slot used for the standalone GET stream. 3221 introduces a type-preserving `_request_stream_key()` (prefixing `i:`/`s:` and explicitly excluding bool-as-int) that keeps int/string ids distinct and guarantees no JSON-RPC id can ever equal `GET_STREAM_KEY`, so it covers both the original duplicate-id case and these two additional collision edge cases that 3063's simpler `str(id)` approach leaves open.

clusters.pick_reason: #3056's _is_optional_str helper narrowly targets `str | None` (the exact corruption case: a plain string that looks like JSON), preserving pre-parse behavior for other str-unions like `str | int` or `str | float` where decoding a numeric-looking string into the non-str member is still the intended behavior. #2032's _should_pre_parse_json instead skips pre-parsing for ANY union whose members are all in {str, int, float, bool, NoneType}, which also disables pre-parsing for `str | int`/`str | float`/`str | bool` unions -- a broader behavior change beyond the reported bug that risks regressing existing union-coercion cases. #3056 also includes an explicit _unwrap_annotated step and documents the str|list[str] contrast case, indicating more careful scoping of the fix.

members.title: fix: skip JSON pre-parsing for str union annotations in pre_parse_json
members.author: adityuhkapoor
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #3056: pre_parse_json in func_metadata.py aggressively json.loads()'s any string value whose annotation is a union containing str, corrupting plain string inputs that happen to look like JSON (e.g. "123", "true", "[1,2]") when the field is typed like `str | None`. members.title: fix(stdio): allow configurable memory stream buffer size
members.author: yaowubarbara
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2654: Both PRs modify the exact same two lines in stdio_server() that construct the read/write anyio memory object streams (currently hardcoded to buffer size 0), and both diffs touch tests/server/test_stdio.py. clusters.pick_reason: Both address unhandled reconnection failure, but via different mechanisms. #2395 sends a JSONRPCError keyed to the original request's id directly through ctx.read_stream_writer using the existing INTERNAL_ERROR convention, scoping the failure to only the affected request. #3098 instead raises a StreamableHTTPError meant to propagate up through the anyio TaskGroup, requiring a new recursive _unwrap_exception helper to dig the typed error back out of anyio ExceptionGroups, plus an unrelated import-style change (dropping the `as _annotations` alias). Raising through the task group has a wider blast radius (risks tearing down the whole group/other in-flight requests) and adds more surface area than reusing the existing per-request error-response pattern.

clusters.pick_reason: 3262 fixes __reduce__ on the base MCPError class itself (using MCPError.__new__ + Exception.__init__ + preserving self.__dict__), so every current and future MCPError subclass is covered generically by one change. 2555 only overrides __reduce__ on UrlElicitationRequiredError, so any other subclass with a non-default constructor (e.g. NoBackChannelError) remains broken - and 3262's own test file was updated to import NoBackChannelError alongside UrlElicitationRequiredError, showing it validates more than one subclass. 2478 introduces a similar dispatcher (_restore_mcp_error) but hardcodes a type check against UrlElicitationRequiredError inside the shared helper, meaning each new subclass with special reconstruction needs would require editing that central function again; it also shows no pickle round-trip tests in the visible diff, whereas both 2555 and 3262 add test coverage under tests/shared/test_exceptions.py.

clusters.pick_reason: 3063 keys `_request_streams` by `str(message.id)`, which collapses JSON-RPC's distinct int `1` and string `"1"` ids into the same key and does nothing to stop a string id equal to `"_GET_stream"` from colliding with the reserved `GET_STREAM_KEY` slot used for the standalone GET stream. 3221 introduces a type-preserving `_request_stream_key()` (prefixing `i:`/`s:` and explicitly excluding bool-as-int) that keeps int/string ids distinct and guarantees no JSON-RPC id can ever equal `GET_STREAM_KEY`, so it covers both the original duplicate-id case and these two additional collision edge cases that 3063's simpler `str(id)` approach leaves open.

Both add a check that rejects/handles the duplicate id before it can clobber the existing routing entry. (2 PRs)
